The data now reaches every section of a document, and a page scope counts within its section.

**Upgrade from any earlier version if your documents have more than one section, or data tokens on a
back page.** Those come out differently, and that is the point of this release: see below. Any other
document comes out as it did. Nothing was removed or renamed in the public API, and the template format
has no new properties.

## Fixed: only the first section was filled

`ReportBinder.Bind` filled the first section and left the others as they were. Everything after the first,
its header, its footer, its body and any sub-document appended with `SubTemplateMode.Append`, went out with
its tokens as typed, its `RepeatOver` lists unrepeated, its `SourceField` pictures empty and its `ShowWhen`
not applied. The document drew without an error. This has been so since sections existed.

Two more of the same kind are fixed with it:

- **The back page** was never filled, though it is documented as holding tokens. A `{Client}` on it now
  comes out as the client's name.
- **A body item with a page scope** stayed in the first section and vanished from any other, leaving its
  room empty. It stays wherever it falls now, in every section.

`TemplateData.Check` follows: it now finds a refused chart in any section, and on the back page.

## Changed: a page scope counts within its section

`PageScope.First` on a header meant the first page of the file, so in any section but the first it never
showed, and an annex could not have a header of its own for its opening page. On an item:

| scope | counts |
|---|---|
| `First`, `Last`, `ExceptFirst`, `ExceptLast`, `Range` | within the item's section, as `{SectionPage}` does |
| `Odd`, `Even` | over the file, being the two sides of a sheet |

A `Watermark` and a `Backdrop` belong to the file, and go on counting over it. With one section the two
countings are the same, so nothing moves.

If you had a header in a second section marked `First` that never appeared, it now appears on that
section's first page.

## Worth checking

A template with several sections may have been written around these faults. Tokens that used to print as
typed are now filled, and a token the data does not answer now follows `BindingOptions.MissingField` there
as it does in the first section: left on the page by default, blanked, or, with `MissingField.Fail`, a
refusal that stops the document. Look at your multi-section documents once before shipping this.
